scanNote:
GRAMMAR REFERENCE, 12-BET (127-bet, oxirgi). Yuqorida o'ngda 'Grammar Reference'.

CHAP USTUN (Unit 14 davomi):
'Tenses change as follows:' Present Simple → Past Simple: "I like it," he said. → He said he liked it. Present Continuous → Past Continuous: "I'm going out," he said. → He said he was going out. Past Simple → Past Perfect: "We met in 1998," he said. → He said they had met in 1998. Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous: "Tom was eating pizza," he said. → He said Tom had been eating pizza. Present Perfect → Past Perfect: "I've known her," he said. → He said he had known her. Will → Would: "I'll tell her," he said. → He said he would tell her. Can → Could: "I can do it," he said. → He said he could do it.
'Personal pronouns and possessive adjectives change according to context.' "I saw you," she said to George. → She said to George that she had seen him.
'REPORTED QUESTIONS': 'Reported questions are introduced with ask, want to know etc. We use affirmative word order and the question mark becomes a full stop. Inverted commas are omitted.' To report a question we use: • ask + question word (who, where, when etc) when the direct question begins with a question word. "What's his name?" She asked. → She asked what his name was. • ask + if/whether when the direct question begins with an auxiliary verb. "Can you help me?" she asked. → She asked if I could help her.
Ko'k-yashil 'UNIT 15'. 'REPORTED ORDERS/INSTRUCTIONS': 'To report orders or instructions we use ask, order etc followed by a to-infinitive.' "Go out!" he said to me. → He ordered me to go out. "Don't go!" he said to me. → He asked me not to go.
'EXCLAMATIONS': 'Exclamations are words or sentences used to express admiration, surprise etc. To form exclamatory sentences we can use how, what (a/an) etc. Exclamatory sentences take an exclamation mark (!) at the end.'

O'NG USTUN:
• We use how + adjective/adverb. 'How nice! How carefully she drives!' • We use what + a/an (+adjective) + singular countable noun. 'What a nice day! What an exciting trip!' • We use what (+adjective) + uncountable/plural nouns. 'What colourful pictures! What awful weather!'
'QUESTION TAGS': • Question tags are short questions at the end of statements. We form them with the auxiliary verb from the main sentence and the appropriate subject pronoun. 'He is tall, isn't he?' • When the verb of the sentence is in the present simple, we use do/does in the question tag. 'He lives in Manchester, doesn't he?' • When the verb of the sentence is in the past simple, we use did in the question tag. 'He left, didn't he?' • A positive statement takes a negative question tag. 'He is from Spain, isn't he?' • A negative statement takes a positive question tag. 'He isn't from France, is he?'
'INTONATION': • When we are sure of the answer, the voice goes down in the question tag. (↘) 'She works at a bank, doesn't she? (sure)' • When we are not sure of the answer, the voice goes up in the question tag. (↗) 'She's got a sister, hasn't she?'
'A/AN - THE': 'We use a/an to talk about something for the first time. We use the to talk about something we have mentioned before. There's a car outside. The car belongs to Mr Jones.' 'We also use the before:' • names of river (the Amazon River), seas (the Black Sea), oceans (the Pacific) and mountain ranges (the Alps). • nationalities (the English), names of families (the Browns). 'We don't use the before:' • proper names (Jane, Rome), names of countries (Britain), names of meals (lunch) or names of sports/games (tennis).

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '127'.

exercises.instructionEn: Tenses change as follows: Present Simple → Past Simple; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Past Simple → Past Perfect; Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect; Will → Would; Can → Could. Personal pronouns and possessive adjectives change according to context.
exercises.instructionUz: Zamonlar shunday o'zgaradi: Present Simple → Past Simple; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Past Simple → Past Perfect; Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect; Will → Would; Can → Could. Kishilik olmoshlari va egalik sifatlari kontekstga qarab o'zgaradi.
exercises.explanationUz:
KO'ChIRMA GAPDA ZAMON O'ZGARIShI
(reporting verb o'tgan zamonda):

  PRESENT SIMPLE → PAST SIMPLE
    "I LIKE it." → He said he
    LIKED it.
  PRESENT CONT. → PAST CONT.
    "I'M GOING out." → He said he
    WAS GOING out.
  PAST SIMPLE → PAST PERFECT
    "We MET in 1998." → He said
    they HAD MET in 1998.
  PAST CONT. → PAST PERFECT CONT.
    "Tom WAS EATING pizza." → He
    said Tom HAD BEEN EATING pizza.
  PRESENT PERFECT → PAST PERFECT
    "I'VE KNOWN her." → He said he
    HAD KNOWN her.
  WILL → WOULD
    "I'LL tell her." → He said he
    WOULD tell her.
  CAN → COULD
    "I CAN do it." → He said he
    COULD do it.

  ⚠ Qoida: BIR QADAM ORQAGA.


OLMOShLAR O'ZGARADI:

  "I saw YOU," she said to George.
  → She said to George that SHE
    had seen HIM.
  I → she; you → him.


⚠ 'ACCORDING TO CONTEXT':

  = kontekstga qarab.


⚠ 'POSSESSIVE ADJECTIVES':

  = egalik sifatlari (my, your,
  his ...).

points.en: Present Simple → Past Simple. "I like it," he said. → He said he liked it. Present Continuous → Past Continuous. "I'm going out," he said. → He said he was going out.
points.uz: Present Simple → Past Simple. "Menga yoqadi", - dedi u. → U yoqishini aytdi. Present Continuous → Past Continuous. "Chiqyapman", - dedi u. → U chiqayotganini aytdi.
points.noteUz: ⚠ like → liked; am going → was going.

points.en: Past Simple → Past Perfect. "We met in 1998," he said. → He said they had met in 1998. Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous. "Tom was eating pizza," he said. → He said Tom had been eating pizza.
points.uz: Past Simple → Past Perfect. "1998 yilda uchrashdik", - dedi u. → U 1998 yilda uchrashganlarini aytdi. Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous. "Tom pitsa yeyayotgan edi", - dedi u. → U Tom pitsa yeyayotganini aytdi.
points.noteUz: ⚠ met → had met; was eating → had been eating.

points.en: Present Perfect → Past Perfect. "I've known her," he said. → He said he had known her. Will → Would. "I'll tell her," he said. → He said he would tell her. Can → Could. "I can do it," he said. → He said he could do it.
points.uz: Present Perfect → Past Perfect. "Uni bilaman", - dedi u. → U uni bilishini aytdi. Will → Would. "Unga aytaman", - dedi u. → U unga aytishini aytdi. Can → Could. "Qila olaman", - dedi u. → U qila olishini aytdi.
points.noteUz: ⚠ have known → had known; will → would; can → could.

points.en: Personal pronouns and possessive adjectives change according to context. "I saw you," she said to George. → She said to George that she had seen him.
points.uz: Kishilik olmoshlari va egalik sifatlari kontekstga qarab o'zgaradi. "Seni ko'rdim", - dedi u Georgega. → U Georgega uni ko'rganini aytdi.

exercises.instructionEn: Reported questions are introduced with ask, want to know etc. We use affirmative word order and the question mark becomes a full stop. Inverted commas are omitted. ask + question word: "What's his name?" She asked. → She asked what his name was. ask + if/whether: "Can you help me?" she asked. → She asked if I could help her.
exercises.instructionUz: Ko'chirma savollar ask, want to know va h.k. bilan kiritiladi. Darak gap tartibini ishlatamiz, so'roq belgisi nuqtaga aylanadi. Qo'shtirnoq tushiriladi. ask + so'roq so'zi: "Uning ismi nima?" - so'radi u. → U uning ismi nima ekanini so'radi. ask + if/whether: "Menga yordam bera olasizmi?" - so'radi u. → U unga yordam bera olishimni so'radi.
exercises.explanationUz:
KO'ChIRMA SAVOLLAR:

  Kiritiladi: ask, want to know,
  wonder ...
  ⚠ DARAK GAP TARTIBI (ega +
  fe'l).
  ⚠ So'roq belgisi (?) → nuqta (.).
  ⚠ Qo'shtirnoq YO'Q.

  1 SO'ROQ SO'ZLI savol → ask +
    so'roq so'zi:
    "What's his name?" →
    She asked WHAT HIS NAME WAS.
    ('what was his name' EMAS!)

  2 HA/YO'Q savol (yordamchi fe'l
    bilan boshlanadi) → ask +
    IF/WHETHER:
    "Can you help me?" →
    She asked IF I COULD help her.


⚠ 'INVERTED COMMAS':

  = qo'shtirnoq (" ").


⚠ 'TO OMIT':

  = tushirib qoldirmoq.


⚠ 'A FULL STOP':

  = nuqta.


⚠ 'WHETHER':

  = ...mi yoki yo'qmi (= if).

points.en: Reported questions are introduced with ask, want to know etc. We use affirmative word order and the question mark becomes a full stop. Inverted commas are omitted.
points.uz: Ko'chirma savollar ask, want to know va h.k. bilan kiritiladi. Darak gap tartibini ishlatamiz, so'roq belgisi nuqtaga aylanadi. Qo'shtirnoq tushiriladi.

points.en: ask + question word (who, where, when etc) when the direct question begins with a question word. "What's his name?" She asked. → She asked what his name was.
points.uz: ask + so'roq so'zi (who, where, when) - to'g'ridan-to'g'ri savol so'roq so'zi bilan boshlansa. "Uning ismi nima?" - so'radi u. → U uning ismi nima ekanini so'radi.

points.en: ask + if/whether when the direct question begins with an auxiliary verb. "Can you help me?" she asked. → She asked if I could help her.
points.uz: ask + if/whether - to'g'ridan-to'g'ri savol yordamchi fe'l bilan boshlansa. "Menga yordam bera olasizmi?" - so'radi u. → U unga yordam bera olishimni so'radi.

sections.title: Unit 15 - Reported Orders; Exclamations; Question Tags; Intonation; Articles
sections.titleUz: 15-unit - Ko'chirma buyruqlar; Undov gaplar; Savol-quyruqlar; Intonatsiya; Artikllar

exercises.instructionEn: Reported orders/instructions: ask, order etc + to-infinitive. "Go out!" → He ordered me to go out. "Don't go!" → He asked me not to go. Exclamations: how + adjective/adverb; what + a/an (+adjective) + singular countable noun; what (+adjective) + uncountable/plural nouns.
exercises.instructionUz: Ko'chirma buyruq/ko'rsatmalar: ask, order va h.k. + to-infinitiv. "Chiq!" → U menga chiqishni buyurdi. "Ketma!" → U mendan ketmaslikni so'radi. Undov gaplar: how + sifat/ravish; what + a/an (+sifat) + birlik sanaladigan ot; what (+sifat) + sanalmaydigan/ko'plik otlar.
exercises.explanationUz:
KO'ChIRMA BUYRUQLAR:

  ask / order / tell + KIM + (NOT)
  TO + FE'L
  "Go out!" → He ORDERED me TO GO
    out.
  "Don't go!" → He ASKED me NOT TO
    GO.


UNDOV GAPLAR:

  Hayrat, ajablanish bildiradi.
  Oxirida undov belgisi (!).

  1 HOW + SIFAT/RAVISh:
    'How nice!'
    'How carefully she drives!'
  2 WHAT + A/AN (+SIFAT) + BIRLIK
    SANALADIGAN OT:
    'What a nice day!'
    'What an exciting trip!'
  3 WHAT (+SIFAT) + SANALMAYDIGAN/
    KO'PLIK OT (a/an YO'Q):
    'What colourful pictures!'
    'What awful weather!'


⚠ 'TO ORDER':

  = buyurmoq.


⚠ 'ADMIRATION':

  = hayrat, qoyil qolish.


⚠ 'AN EXCLAMATION MARK':

  = undov belgisi (!).

points.en: To report orders or instructions we use ask, order etc followed by a to-infinitive. "Go out!" he said to me. → He ordered me to go out. "Don't go!" he said to me. → He asked me not to go.
points.uz: Buyruq yoki ko'rsatmalarni ko'chirish uchun ask, order va h.k. + to-infinitiv ishlatamiz. "Chiq!" - dedi u menga. → U menga chiqishni buyurdi. "Ketma!" - dedi u menga. → U mendan ketmaslikni so'radi.

points.en: Exclamations are words or sentences used to express admiration, surprise etc. To form exclamatory sentences we can use how, what (a/an) etc. Exclamatory sentences take an exclamation mark (!) at the end.
points.uz: Undov gaplar - hayrat, ajablanish va h.k. bildiruvchi so'z yoki gaplar. Undov gaplarni how, what (a/an) va h.k. bilan yasaymiz. Undov gaplar oxirida undov belgisi (!) bo'ladi.

points.en: We use how + adjective/adverb. How nice! How carefully she drives! We use what + a/an (+adjective) + singular countable noun. What a nice day! What an exciting trip! We use what (+adjective) + uncountable/plural nouns. What colourful pictures! What awful weather!
points.uz: How + sifat/ravish ishlatamiz. Qanday yaxshi! U qanday ehtiyotkor haydaydi! What + a/an (+sifat) + birlik sanaladigan ot ishlatamiz. Qanday yaxshi kun! Qanday hayajonli sayohat! What (+sifat) + sanalmaydigan/ko'plik otlar ishlatamiz. Qanday rangli suratlar! Qanday dahshatli ob-havo!

exercises.instructionEn: Question tags are short questions at the end of statements, formed with the auxiliary verb from the main sentence and the appropriate subject pronoun. He is tall, isn't he? Present simple: do/does. He lives in Manchester, doesn't he? Past simple: did. He left, didn't he? Positive statement → negative tag; negative statement → positive tag. Intonation: sure → voice goes down (↘); not sure → voice goes up (↗).
exercises.instructionUz: Savol-quyruqlar - gap oxiridagi qisqa savollar, asosiy gapdagi yordamchi fe'l va mos ega olmoshi bilan yasaladi. U baland bo'yli, shundaymi? Hozirgi oddiy: do/does. U Manchesterda yashaydi, shundaymi? O'tgan oddiy: did. U ketdi, shundaymi? Ijobiy gap → inkor quyruq; inkor gap → ijobiy quyruq. Intonatsiya: ishonch → ovoz pasayadi (↘); ishonchsiz → ovoz ko'tariladi (↗).
exercises.explanationUz:
SAVOL-QUYRUQLAR (QUESTION TAGS):

  Gap OXIRIDA qisqa savol.
  Yordamchi fe'l + OLMOSh.

  'be' bilan: 'He IS tall, ISN'T
    HE?'
  PRESENT SIMPLE → do/does:
    'He LIVES in Manchester,
     DOESN'T HE?'
  PAST SIMPLE → did:
    'He LEFT, DIDN'T HE?'

  IJOBIY gap → INKOR quyruq:
    'He IS from Spain, ISN'T he?'
  INKOR gap → IJOBIY quyruq:
    'He ISN'T from France, IS he?'


INTONATSIYa:

  ↘ PASAYADI - ishonchim komil,
    tasdiq kutaman:
    'She works at a bank, doesn't
     she?' ↘ (bilaman)
  ↗ KO'TARILADI - ishonchim yo'q,
    haqiqiy savol:
    "She's got a sister, hasn't
     she?" ↗ (bilmayman)


⚠ 'APPROPRIATE':

  = mos.


⚠ 'Manchester':

  = Manchester (Angliya shahri).

points.en: Question tags are short questions at the end of statements. We form them with the auxiliary verb from the main sentence and the appropriate subject pronoun. He is tall, isn't he?
points.uz: Savol-quyruqlar - gap oxiridagi qisqa savollar. Ularni asosiy gapdagi yordamchi fe'l va mos ega olmoshi bilan yasaymiz. U baland bo'yli, shundaymi?

points.en: When the verb of the sentence is in the present simple, we use do/does in the question tag. He lives in Manchester, doesn't he? When the verb of the sentence is in the past simple, we use did in the question tag. He left, didn't he?
points.uz: Gap fe'li hozirgi oddiy zamonda bo'lsa, savol-quyruqda do/does ishlatamiz. U Manchesterda yashaydi, shundaymi? Gap fe'li o'tgan oddiy zamonda bo'lsa, savol-quyruqda did ishlatamiz. U ketdi, shundaymi?
points.noteUz: ⚠ lives → doesn't he; left → didn't he.

points.en: A positive statement takes a negative question tag. He is from Spain, isn't he? A negative statement takes a positive question tag. He isn't from France, is he?
points.uz: Ijobiy gap inkor savol-quyruq oladi. U Ispaniyadan, shundaymi? Inkor gap ijobiy savol-quyruq oladi. U Fransiyadan emas, shundaymi?

points.en: When we are sure of the answer, the voice goes down in the question tag (↘). She works at a bank, doesn't she? (sure) When we are not sure of the answer, the voice goes up in the question tag (↗). She's got a sister, hasn't she?
points.uz: Javobga ishonchimiz komil bo'lsa, savol-quyruqda ovoz pasayadi (↘). U bankda ishlaydi, shundaymi? (ishonch) Javobga ishonchimiz komil bo'lmasa, savol-quyruqda ovoz ko'tariladi (↗). Uning singlisi bor, shundaymi?

exercises.instructionEn: A/An - The. We use a/an to talk about something for the first time. We use the to talk about something we have mentioned before. There's a car outside. The car belongs to Mr Jones. We also use the before names of rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, nationalities, names of families. We don't use the before proper names, names of countries, meals, sports/games.
exercises.instructionUz: A/An - The. Biror narsa haqida birinchi marta gapirganda a/an ishlatamiz. Oldin tilga olgan narsa haqida gapirganda the ishlatamiz. Tashqarida mashina bor. Mashina janob Jonesniki. 'The' ni daryo, dengiz, okean, tog' tizmalari, millatlar, oila nomlari oldida ham ishlatamiz. Atoqli otlar, mamlakat, ovqat, sport/o'yin nomlari oldida 'the' ishlatmaymiz.
exercises.explanationUz:
ARTIKLLAR: A/AN - THE.

  A/AN - BIRINChI MARTA:
    "There's A car outside."
  THE - OLDIN TILGA OLINGAN:
    'THE car belongs to Mr Jones.'


'THE' IShLATILADI:

  • daryolar: the Amazon River
  • dengizlar: the Black Sea
  • okeanlar: the Pacific
  • tog' tizmalari: the Alps
  • millatlar: the English
  • oila nomlari: the Browns


'THE' IShLATILMAYDI:

  • atoqli otlar: Jane, Rome
  • mamlakatlar: Britain
  • ovqatlar: lunch
  • sport/o'yinlar: tennis

  ⚠ Istisnolar: the USA, the UK
  (ko'plik/qo'shma nomlar).


⚠ 'TO BELONG TO':

  = ...ga tegishli bo'lmoq.


⚠ 'A MOUNTAIN RANGE':

  = tog' tizmasi.


⚠ 'A PROPER NAME':

  = atoqli ot.

points.en: We use a/an to talk about something for the first time. We use the to talk about something we have mentioned before. There's a car outside. The car belongs to Mr Jones.
points.uz: Biror narsa haqida birinchi marta gapirganda a/an ishlatamiz. Oldin tilga olgan narsa haqida gapirganda the ishlatamiz. Tashqarida mashina bor. Mashina janob Jonesniki.

points.en: We also use the before: names of rivers (the Amazon River), seas (the Black Sea), oceans (the Pacific) and mountain ranges (the Alps); nationalities (the English), names of families (the Browns).
points.uz: 'The' ni bular oldida ham ishlatamiz: daryolar (the Amazon River), dengizlar (the Black Sea), okeanlar (the Pacific) va tog' tizmalari (the Alps); millatlar (the English), oila nomlari (the Browns).

points.en: We don't use the before: proper names (Jane, Rome), names of countries (Britain), names of meals (lunch) or names of sports/games (tennis).
points.uz: 'The' ni bular oldida ishlatmaymiz: atoqli otlar (Jane, Rome), mamlakat nomlari (Britain), ovqat nomlari (lunch) yoki sport/o'yin nomlari (tennis).
